findings: Branch environment varies by location; cleanliness is inconsistent and signage differs between branches.
New-patient registration is lengthy because the registration document is 2–3 pages.
Telecalling team is making regular follow-up calls to patients.
Patient reviews are encouraged, but the review-request process is not yet fully structured and timely across branches.
Basic follow-up exists, but a more structured patient-retention process is needed to improve repeat visits and long-term engagement.
Branch addresses, phone numbers, daily posts and therapy descriptions are available, but photos and Q&A are missing.
Automation exists, but patients may wait to connect and customised replies can be delayed until the end of the day.
Positive and negative reviews are reportedly responded to properly, but review volume is low.
A content calendar exists, but posting is repetitive and heavily focused on disease-related tips; the assessment recommends a more balanced mix of disease, therapy and patient-recovery content.
Detailed patient-review videos exist, but they are not released on a regular schedule.
The assessment states that Swasi pricing is higher than competitors.
Competitors are known, but there is no separate team/process monitoring competitor growth and changes.
No documented baseline was found for brand-equity metrics such as NPS, awareness, referral rate, review rating and repeat visit rate.
